title: Pre-Decision Human Review Gate Pattern
description: A pattern in which an automated adverse decision about an individual's rights or benefits cannot take effect until a qualified human has reviewed the specific case, with a completed data protection impact assessment and documented legal basis in place before the system is used at all.

history.note: Normalized US/UK spelling variants to the American-English house style (schema field names, e.g. organizations_involved, are already American; majority framework citations - NIST, FTC, EEOC, FCRA, BIPA - are American sources).

problem: Automated systems that flag individuals for adverse action (a fraud investigation, a debt notice, a downgraded exam grade) are often deployed with an appeals process available only after the adverse action has already taken effect, by which point the harm — reputational, financial, or otherwise — has already occurred.
solution: Require a documented legal basis and a completed data protection impact assessment before the system processes any individual's data; require a qualified human to review and affirmatively approve each adverse decision before it takes effect, with visibility into the automated system's specific basis for flagging that individual; and classify the system against relevant high-risk categories (e.g. welfare eligibility, education, essential services) so the appropriate level of scrutiny is applied from the start.
applicability: Any automated or algorithmic system used by a government body, or any organization, to make or heavily inform a decision that adversely affects an individual's welfare eligibility, education outcomes, immigration status, or similar legal rights.
consequences: Pre-decision human review at scale requires enough trained staff to meaningfully engage with each flagged case rather than rubber-stamping the system's output; a DPIA and legal-basis review add lead time before a system can be deployed or materially changed.

citations.title: Final Report — Royal Commission into the Robodebt Scheme
citations.publisher: Royal Commission into the Robodebt Scheme (Australian Government)

relationships.reason: Classifying the system against Annex III high-risk categories is a concrete step in this pattern.
The pattern's required DPIA directly satisfies this control.
The pattern's output is a completed data protection impact assessment.
